title: to the moon
text: I don't normally write game reviews, but I guess 'To The Moon' isn't really a game, more a interactive story. I've been meaning to play this for a while now, so when it was on the sale I grabbed a copy. And I have to say, it's the best £1.50 I have ever spend. I would have no problem spending the full price. In short the story, the music, the art style, the pacing are all fantastic. I have read loads of reviews were people have said the story made them cry. At first I wasn't convinced I would have an emotional attachment to the characters in such a short space of time - I WAS WRONG. Although I didn't cry, there were moments where my heart was in my throat! Something I haven't experienced in a videogame for a long time! This is the best game I have played in a long time. I recommend it to everyone. If you can, please play it in one sitting. I managed to complete it in just under 4.5 hours. Trust me, you will find it hard to put down. I hope you enjoy it as much as I did.

title: toki tori
text: Toki Tori is a puzzle game with very simple controls.  Using only the mouse to point and click directions to your avatar, and using the tools provided in limited supply, you need to navigate your avatar to each egg in the level.  It is a really simple concept with simple to use tools.  That is where the true beauty of the game lies.  The first few levels warm you up to the control scheme and tools, but it gets really tricky really fast.  The normal levels aren't all that hard, but the hard levels had me wracking my brain for a bit of time, looking for any tiny loophole; anything to exploit.  The game goes from fun to maddeningly frustrating, but not in a hurry to punish.  If you love simple puzzle platformers, you definitely should give this a shot.  If you are looking for an action platformer, this is definitely not what you are looking for.

If you like a challenge, try the no-med pack run or only saving at the old playstation locations. I would note though, that I have experienced crashes, though not often. title: tomb raider ii
text: First off, keep in mind that this game is 19 years old and will require some minor tweaking if you want it to look at least semi-decent. I absolutely don't recommend playing it as is, it looks really bad. Download and install the widescreen patch first, then download this patch if the game displays a Windows border in fullscreen mode . The cutscenes are interlaced and look awful, but I remember them looking just as bad back in 1997. Now you're all set to play what many consider to be the best Tomb Raider game ever made. Compared to its predecessor, Tomb Raider 2 is much more action oriented. Personally I always liked this game more than the original, even if the combat is still the same lackluster "run around like a headless chicken while holding the Fire button" kind of thing. Other than being combat heavy, it's your standard classic Tomb Raider. Puzzles, platforming, deadly traps, mysterious artifacts, it's all there. Even after all these years, TR2 still has a charm that cannot be matched. There's something about its low poly enemies and silence only occasionally interrupted by bursts of music that makes this game scarier than the latest photorealistic reboot. I'm probably biased since this is a game I've completed many, many times since the 90's and I consider it to be the best game in the entire Tomb Raider franchise, but to me everything about it is perfect. Its controls are outdated but solid and you get used to them quickly. The sound design is amazing, the atmosphere creepy. The levels are huge with lots of nooks and cranies to explore and secrets to discover. Even if you're not an old Tomb Raider fan and you've only just discovered the franchise, do yourself a favor and play this game to see how the legend started. Oh, and whatever you do, do NOT press F12 while playing. It'll force the game into windowed mode and cutscenes will stop working. You'll then have to quit the game, go back to Steam and change the game settings back to fullscreen.

text: This game is a classic. It was one of the games that helped spawn the mighty fandom of the Tomb Raider franchise. It's graphics were likely pretty good for the time, but I only played it a few years later, and I still loved it. The water is particularly impressive considering it was released in 1997. However, I can't recommend buying this. The reason why is that it appears they did nothing, or next to nothing, to make it more capable of running on modern machines. When I first launched it, the setup appeared behind the main window, so I couldn't edit it. I didn't even know it was supposed to appear, so I just clicked return, and the game loaded up, with most of the right side black, and part of the left side cut off. I checked for settings, to no avail. Like a few extremely old games, the video setup is separate from the game (and not exactly intuitive to access from within Steam). Opening it, I wasn't able to change the full screen resolution from 640x480 for some reason. After disabling my second monitor, and setting my main monitor to 800x600 (the smallest resolution where I could still see the apply button), I managed to get the game to appear correctly. A bit of a hassle to say the least. I also installed the widescreen patch. After restarting to re-enable my second monitor, I then tried it in windowed mode. Steam absolutely will not launch it in windowed mode. I had to open it from the exe. It was a travesty. It kept switching the resolution to 640x480 despite being in windowed mode, and was impossible to play. But, somehow, after that, I restarted, and tried it again from steam, and it magically just worked, in full screen mode, without disabling my second monitor. It was still in 640x480 unfortunately, but there was no black bar on one side, and it appeared correctly. I played it for a few minutes before my computer switched to another application on it's own, because the standard keys are set for alt to be the jump key. So, I will play through this game once more, and keep it on my Steam to occasionally play, but I really don't suggest anyone else buys it. They didn't do a thing to try to remove any bugs or anything from what I can tell. They simply took the old retail version and packaged it for steam. Frankly, I would be embarrassed if I worked for them. They should either hand the code to some of their team to squash some bugs occasionally, and clean up the code, or open source it, so maybe someone out there somewhere will choose to clean up the code for them. This game is barely playable on a modern machine. I'm likely gonna have to set up a virtual machine just to play this and a few other old games giving me trouble.

title: tomb raider ii
text: Tomb Raider II brings back the iconic charismatic archaeologist, Lara Croft, on another epic journey around the globe to investigate the legend around the Dagger of Xian. Her second adventure takes her along the Great Wall of China, the snowy terrains of Tibet, Italy’s city of Venice and a sunken shipwreck, accompanied by more complex series of jumping puzzles and death traps, lever activated time puzzles and the merciless killing of treasure hunting goons and exotic animals that stand in her path. The game grants Lara the ability to climb ladders and craggy walls, to roll in the air and underwater for trickier puzzles, and to drive vehicles such as speedboats and snowmobiles around certain levels in the game, which can be incredibly fun and very tedious at the same time. Flares have been thrown into the game to allow Lara to explore particularly dark areas with ease, which come in handy for some of the later levels, along with new weapons packing serious firepower like the M16 assault rifle, a grenade launcher and automatic dual pistols (which replace the dual magnums that were available in TR1), along with all weapons within the previous game. Enemies now have the intelligence to climb surfaces in order to reach Lara and carry pretty damaging weaponry, making combat somewhat more difficult, especially when they corner the player in tight spaces. Meaning there will be more ammo to find, a few more medicine packs to collect, and there are 3 secrets to find throughout each level; the gold, jade and silver dragons. For those who have played Tomb Raider I, you will be pleased to hear that instead of having to save your progress at a save crystal and having to restart tedious levels every time Lara plummets to her death from that point, Tomb Raider II allows you to save your progress from your save manual whenever and wherever. It makes life much, much easier. All environments and graphics appear to have been enhanced both in colour and in quality in this game, ultimately keeping movable blocks and secret areas better hidden, so it’s very easy to overlook a potential secret or an area full of loot if you aren’t actively exploring the entire level. The soundtrack in the game has been heavily built off its predecessor, only playing on certain cues like when the protagonist steps into the path of a rolling boulder, as it did in the previous game. Another change to be noted is the change in voice actress for our fearless protagonist. Personally, I felt that her new voice fitted Lara better as she sounds much more experienced and capable of handling herself like a badass, whereas, her voice in TR1 portrayed her to be more of an arrogant adolescent. The tutorial area in Lara Croft’s manor has developed greatly from its elder. The crates blocking most of the large manor have now been removed, inviting the player to explore the charming home more thoroughly. The gymnasium and the swimming pool reappear in this game, but with much obstacles to manoeuvre through and a prettier pool to swim around in. Here is where you are introduced to Winston, Lara’s old butler who is intent on following her around the house while groaning and carrying a tray of rattling tea cups. On the odd occasion when I accidently ran into him, there is a chance that he will break wind. It can be pretty fun for a while, but eventually having him dog you around the manor will grow tedious. My solution was to have him follow me to the meat locker in the kitchen, wait for him to follow a certain distance behind, then perform a well-timed leap out of the area, and lock him in. I found watching him try to walk through the door grunting and groaning to be quite amusing. Cruel, but amusing. Lara can now venture outside the manor and explore the maze behind it. The main section behind the maze is an assault course the player can now test out their skills on obstacles that are a bit more challenging than the gym. All in all, if you’re looking for a game where you can relax and enjoy shooting lead into your enemies, but still challenging enough that it keeps you wondering about any potential death traps around the corner, Tomb Raider II is a classic game with plenty of everything and is generally fun to play, even when using the Playstation controls, although the PC controls are much more fluid.
